title: The Northeastern Sector
mood: The dome is torn, a teacher falls, and two rivals have to fight side by side.

hero.alt: A huge gray Ender lifts its head against an orange evening sky, more Enders drifting down behind it.

segs.t: The portal spat Layla out into smoke. It smelled of hot metal and real fire. The VR pods had never smelled of anything.
At the avenue’s end the dome came down to the ground, a wall of pale hexagons. Enders had torn a hole in it, eight meters wide and two high.

An Ender was forcing its head and shoulders through. Joe’s VR Enders had stood three meters tall. This one would have looked into a second-floor window. Its gray plates ground together, and the sound went into Layla’s back teeth.

media.alt: Giant black claws rake through the glowing hexagons of the dome above the city skyline.

segs.t: People ran past her the other way. Her heart was going so hard she checked her hands. They were not shaking.
“I’ll take down the Enders!” she said, to hear how it sounded.
“Good,” said Fanny, drawing a blade from the case at her hip.
Twenty meters ahead, Joe was turning the crowd into a side street with one arm.
“Everybody fall back now!”
A little girl in a red dress stood crying in the middle of the pavement, holding a pink rabbit by one ear. Joe went to her and knelt.
“Don’t be scared kiddo, everything’s gonna be alright.”

media.alt: Under the cracking dome, Professor Joe waves the crowd back while a little girl in a red dress runs past him.
Joe kneels to the crying girl and her pink rabbit and tells her not to be scared.

segs.t: The Ender heaved. The front of the corner building came down in a slab. Joe turned his back and covered the girl and the rabbit. The slab struck him across the shoulders.
A woman swept the girl up. Joe lay still, one hand open on the stones. The Ender had not even looked.
“Professor Joe!” Fanny was beside him before the name was out.
“You take Professor Joe somewhere safe,” said Layla, walking toward the hole. “I’ll kill this freak!”

media.alt: Layla, furious, raises her cannon and says she will kill this freak.

segs.t: “Wait! You won’t be able to take it out alone!”
“What’s your plan, then?”
“Cover me! I’ll look for a weak spot around its neck!”

Its chest was plated shut. By Joe’s rule it opened only when the thing struck, and nobody wanted it striking at the crowd. The neck was the only opening. Fanny was right. Layla did not intend to say so.
“No way! You cover me instead!”
Fanny looked at her for one breath. “Whatever, let’s do this!”
Roger, late out of the portal, got an arm under Joe’s shoulders and dragged him toward the side street. Layla saw it and kept walking.

Fanny went up on her hip thrusters, her cable unreeling in a shining line. Layla set the cannon on her shoulder. A row of cyan cells on the stock showed the charge. Her thumb found the dial and stopped.
The numbers looked right. They had looked right before. She turned the dial down two notches.

media.alt: Layla swings her long white cannon up to her shoulder among the towers, the evening sun behind her.

segs.t: “Use the big shot!” Fanny’s voice said in her ear.
“I’m saving it!”
“For what?”
“For something big!”

Layla fired. Thin white bolts hit the elbow of the arm holding the lip, quick and true. The Ender turned its head to find what was stinging it. The collar plates rose, and a dark seam opened under the skull.
“I’m not covering you,” said Layla. “I’m shooting where it happens to be looking.”
“Thanks,” said Fanny, and dropped onto its back with both blades.
They went in to the hilt. The Ender stopped. Fanny’s cable took its shoulder, and she hauled it down along the dome wall, away from the street.

media.alt: Under a caption about the first time the two joined forces, Fanny drives in with blades and cable while Layla fires her cannon.

segs.t: It had taken under a minute. After the first call, neither had given an order. Fanny had never once been in her line. Layla noticed, and did not like having noticed.
Farther along the wall, two bright figures hung in the air with wings spread and drones circling them in step. Roger had stopped at the corner to hitch Joe higher.
“That’s Guinevere and Vexana!” he said. “They’ve got the other end!”
“I know who they are,” said Layla.

media.alt: Vexana, a girl with long black hair and violet eyes in the Selrick uniform, frowns as she fights.

segs.t: The crowd went quiet, every face turned the same way. Layla turned with it.
Through the dome, out on the sand, something gold stood up. It bent its long head toward the hole. The low sun lit one flank orange. Light began to gather in its chest.
None of Joe’s three ranks had been gold.

media.alt: A gold giant's head and glowing eyes loom behind the dome's blue hexagons.

segs.t: A child’s voice carried clearly from the front of the crowd.
“Mommy, what’s that?”
